title: Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — Adams County Department of Human Services — 11860 Pecos St - Adams County
summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:  Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter

fields.organization name: Adams County Department of Human Services
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:  Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below    'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. Household Size Monthly Gross Income for the 2025-2026 Season                 60% of State Median Income    1 - $3,607  2 - $4,717  3 - $5,827  4 - $6,938  5 - $8,048  6 - $9,158  7 - $9,366  8 - $9,574  Each Additional Person $208       Area Served: Adams County
fields.access method: Apply online. Visit the website to download a paper application and drop off at the local DHS office or mail/email to the county to process. Call to request a mailed paper application, to apply over the phone, or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Proof of citizenship if born outside of the US   Proof of all monthly household income    Receipts for all expenses claimed on profit and loss statement, if self-employed  Copy of most recent heating bill or recent rent receipt, if heat is included with rent
fields.hours of operation: November 1st - April 30th (Application Open); Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

title: Adult Diabetes Education Classes (DSMES) — Adams County Health Department — 7000 N Broadway - Adams County
summary: Provides a series of interactive diabetes group classes for individuals with a diagnosis of diabetes to build the skills and knowledge to make healthier life choices and manage their diabetes. Class topics include:   What is diabetes  Facts and myths about diabetes  Monitoring blood sugar  How to read and use blood sugar numbers  Medicines and how they work in the body  The basics of insulin and different types  Healthy eating strategies  Managing diabetes long-term  Physical activity   Individuals can attend 1 session or every session and can bring a friend or family member for support.

title: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) — Adams County Health Department — 1401 W 122nd Ave - Adams County
summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable
fields.hours of operation: Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 12:30 p.m., 1 p.m. - 5 p.m.

fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. fields.service summary: Assists disabled veterans in applying for a 50% exemption on the first $200,000 of actual value for their primary residence.

title: Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — Arapahoe County Department of Human Services — 14980 E Alameda Dr - Arapahoe County
summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:   Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter

fields.organization name: Arapahoe County Department of Human Services
fields.physical address: 14980 E Alameda Dr, 1st Fl, Aurora, CO, 80012
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:   Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below    'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. Household Size Monthly Gross Income for the 2025-2026 Season                 60% of State Median Income    1 - $3,607  2 - $4,717  3 - $5,827  4 - $6,938  5 - $8,048  6 - $9,158  7 - $9,366  8 - $9,574  Each Additional Person $208    Area Served: Arapahoe County
fields.access method: Apply online. Visit the website to download a paper application and drop off at the local DHS office or mail/email to the county to process. Call to request a mailed paper application, to apply over the phone, or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Proof of citizenship if born outside of the US   Proof of all monthly household income    If self-employed, receipts for all expenses claimed on profit and loss statement   Copy of most recent heating bill or recent rent receipt, if heat is included with rent
fields.hours of operation: November 1st - April 30th (Application Open); Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.
